questions.subject: biology
questions.question: In transverse section, a typical angiosperm anther appears tetragonal. How many microsporangia does such an anther have?

solution.key_concept: A typical anther is bilobed and dithecous, so it is tetrasporangiate.
steps: A typical anther has 2 lobes.
Each lobe has 2 thecae.
Microsporangia per anther = $2 \times 2 = 4$, one at each corner of the tetragonal section.
solution.why_not_others: 2 is the number of lobes, or of thecae per lobe. 8 doubles the correct count. 1 ignores the bilobed, dithecous structure.
solution.common_trap: Counting only the lobes (2) instead of the microsporangia.
solution.time_saving_tip: Tetragonal section means four corners, with one microsporangium at each corner.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a plant with the number of ovules in its ovary?

solution.key_concept: The number of ovules per ovary ranges from one to many.
steps: Wheat, paddy and mango have a single ovule.
Papaya, watermelon and orchids have many ovules.
Only the mango pairing is correct.
solution.why_not_others: Papaya and orchids have many ovules, not one. Wheat has a single ovule, not many.
solution.common_trap: Assuming a large fruit such as mango must contain many ovules.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the gynoecium of Papaver?
options: Multicarpellary and apocarpous, as in Michelia
Bilobed and dithecous with four sporangia

solution.key_concept: Multicarpellary gynoecia are either syncarpous (fused carpels) or apocarpous (free carpels).
steps: Papaver has many carpels that are fused together.
Fused carpels make the gynoecium syncarpous.
Michelia is the example of an apocarpous gynoecium.
solution.why_not_others: Papaver is not monocarpellary. Apocarpous describes Michelia. 'Bilobed and dithecous' describes an anther, not a gynoecium.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging the examples Papaver (syncarpous) and Michelia (apocarpous).

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: A typical angiosperm anther has only two microsporangia, one in each lobe.
statements.R: A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed, and each lobe has two thecae.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: A dithecous, bilobed anther has 4 microsporangia.
steps: Each lobe has 2 thecae, so R is true.
A bilobed anther therefore has $2 \times 2 = 4$ microsporangia.
A claims only 2, so A is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so any option that calls A true is ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Equating the number of lobes with the number of microsporangia.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: The stigma serves as the landing platform for pollen, and the ovules are attached to the placenta inside the ovarian cavity.
statements.II: Wheat, paddy and watermelon are all examples of plants whose ovary contains a single ovule.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Parts of the pistil and the number of ovules in different plants.
steps: The stigma is the landing platform for pollen, and the ovules arise from the placenta in the locule, so I is correct.
Wheat and paddy have a single ovule, but watermelon has many ovules, so II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II fails because of watermelon, which has many ovules. Statement I is fully correct.
solution.common_trap: Reading the first two correct examples in Statement II and missing the wrong third one.
solution.time_saving_tip: Check every example in a list; one wrong item makes the whole statement false.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Development of male and female gametophytes
questions.question: Which wall layer of the microsporangium nourishes the developing pollen grains?

solution.key_concept: The tapetum is the innermost, nutritive wall layer of the microsporangium.
steps: From outside inward, the wall layers are epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and tapetum.
The outer three layers protect the sporangium and help in dehiscence.
The tapetum, whose cells have dense cytoplasm and often more than one nucleus, nourishes the pollen.
solution.why_not_others: The epidermis, endothecium and middle layers are protective layers that help dehiscence; they do not nourish the pollen.
solution.common_trap: Choosing the endothecium because its name sounds like an inner layer.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Development of male and female gametophytes
questions.question: What is the minimum number of meiotic divisions required to produce 200 pollen grains?

solution.key_concept: One microspore mother cell divides by meiosis to give a tetrad of 4 pollen grains.
steps: One meiosis gives 4 pollen grains.
Meioses needed = $\frac{200}{4} = 50$.
solution.why_not_others: 200 assumes one meiosis per grain. 100 assumes each meiosis gives only 2 grains. 25 wrongly divides by 8.
solution.common_trap: Applying the female rule of one functional product per meiosis to the male side.
solution.time_saving_tip: Male side: divide by 4. Female side: one meiosis per embryo sac.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Development of male and female gametophytes
questions.question: Formation of one mature embryo sac from a megaspore mother cell involves which of the following?

solution.key_concept: Development of the embryo sac is monosporic, with three free-nuclear mitoses.
steps: The megaspore mother cell undergoes 1 meiosis to give 4 megaspores, and 3 of them degenerate.
The functional megaspore undergoes 3 free-nuclear mitoses: $1 \to 2 \to 4 \to 8$ nuclei.
Total: 1 meiosis and 3 mitoses.
solution.why_not_others: 4 meioses confuses the number of megaspores with the number of divisions. 8 mitoses confuses the number of nuclei with the number of divisions. 2 mitoses would give only 4 nuclei.
solution.common_trap: Counting the final 8 nuclei as 8 divisions.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Development of male and female gametophytes
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Divides to form two male gametes

solution.key_concept: Structure of the pollen grain wall and the cells of a mature pollen grain.
steps: Exine is made of sporopollenin: A-II.
Intine is made of cellulose and pectin: B-I.
Germ pores are regions of the exine that lack sporopollenin: C-III.
The generative cell divides to form two male gametes: D-IV.
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps the compositions of the exine and intine. Option 2 swaps the germ pore and generative cell. Option 4 swaps the exine and germ pore.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the compositions of the exine and intine.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Development of male and female gametophytes
questions.question: Which of the following statements about gametophyte development in angiosperms are correct?

statements.A: The megaspore mother cell lies in the micropylar region of the nucellus.
statements.B: Of the four megaspores formed, three degenerate, so embryo sac development is monosporic.
statements.C: The mature embryo sac is 8-nucleate and 8-celled.
statements.D: The egg apparatus, made of two synergids and one egg, lies at the chalazal end.
statements.E: More than 60% of angiosperms shed their pollen at the 2-celled stage.

solution.key_concept: Megasporogenesis, the organisation of the embryo sac and the stage of pollen shedding.
steps: A is correct: the megaspore mother cell is in the micropylar region of the nucellus.
B is correct: only one megaspore is functional, so development is monosporic.
C is wrong: the embryo sac is 8-nucleate but 7-celled, because the 2 polar nuclei share one central cell.
D is wrong: the egg apparatus lies at the micropylar end; the antipodals are at the chalazal end.
E is correct: over 60% of angiosperms shed pollen at the 2-celled stage.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, B and E only
solution.why_not_others: Every other option includes C or D, and both of these are false.
solution.common_trap: Assuming 8 nuclei means 8 cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which of the following plants produces cleistogamous flowers?

solution.key_concept: Cleistogamous flowers never open, so they are invariably autogamous.
steps: The notes give Viola, Oxalis and Commelina as examples of cleistogamous flowers.
Commelina is the only one of these among the options.
solution.why_not_others: Vallisneria is water-pollinated, maize is wind-pollinated, and Yucca is pollinated by a moth. All three rely on external agents.
solution.common_trap: Picking an unusual plant without checking whether its flowers actually open.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember the cleistogamous examples as V-O-C: Viola, Oxalis, Commelina.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which of the following aquatic plants is pollinated by insects or wind rather than by water?

solution.key_concept: Not every aquatic plant is water-pollinated.
steps: Vallisneria, Hydrilla and Zostera are water-pollinated.
Water lily and water hyacinth are aquatic but are pollinated by insects or wind.
solution.why_not_others: The other three are standard examples of water pollination.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that every aquatic plant is water-pollinated.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Geitonogamy is best described as pollination that is
options: the transfer of pollen to the stigma of the same flower
the transfer of pollen from a different plant, bringing genetically different pollen
functionally cross-pollination but genetically similar to autogamy
always confined to flowers that never open

solution.key_concept: In geitonogamy, pollen comes from another flower of the same plant.
steps: The pollen travels between two flowers, so the process is functionally cross-pollination.
The pollen comes from the same plant, so genetically it is like autogamy.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): functionally cross-pollination but genetically similar to autogamy
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 describes autogamy. Option 2 describes xenogamy. Option 4 describes cleistogamy.
solution.common_trap: Treating geitonogamy as genetic cross-pollination.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Cleistogamous flowers assure seed set even in the absence of pollinators.
statements.R: Cleistogamous flowers never open, so they are invariably autogamous.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Cleistogamy guarantees self-pollination.
steps: Cleistogamous flowers stay closed, so the pollen falls on the stigma of the same flower (R is true).
Because pollination happens inside the flower, no pollinator is needed and seed set is assured (A is true).
R directly explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true and causally linked, so options 2, 3 and 4 do not fit.
solution.common_trap: Marking option 2 without checking that the closed flower is exactly why seed set is assured.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In Vallisneria, pollen grains are released on the surface of water, and the long-stalked female flowers reach the surface.
statements.II: In seagrasses such as Zostera, long ribbon-like pollen grains are carried inside the water.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Water pollination can take place on the water surface or below it.
steps: Vallisneria shows surface pollination, with long-stalked female flowers reaching the surface, so I is correct.
In seagrasses, ribbon-like pollen is carried inside the water, so II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements match the notes exactly, so no option that calls either one incorrect can be right.
solution.common_trap: Thinking all water pollination happens on the surface and marking II as incorrect.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which of the following plants prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy?

solution.key_concept: Dioecy prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy.
steps: Papaya is dioecious, with male and female flowers on separate plants.
Pollen must therefore come from another plant, which rules out both autogamy and geitonogamy.
solution.why_not_others: Castor and maize are monoecious and prevent autogamy only. Viola has cleistogamous flowers, which are autogamous.
solution.common_trap: Believing that monoecious maize or castor also prevents geitonogamy.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: In an artificial hybridization programme, emasculation is NOT required when the female parent bears
options: chasmogamous bisexual flowers with exposed anthers and stigma
bisexual flowers in which the anther and stigma are placed at different positions

solution.key_concept: Emasculation means removing anthers from bisexual flowers before they dehisce.
steps: Emasculation is needed only where anthers are present, that is, in bisexual flowers.
Unisexual female flowers have no anthers, so they are only bagged and then rebagged after pollination.
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 2 and 4 all describe bisexual flowers, which carry anthers and so must be emasculated.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that different positioning of anther and stigma removes the need for emasculation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: After entering the ovule through the micropyle, the pollen tube enters
options: the egg directly through the chalaza
an antipodal cell at the chalazal end
one of the synergids through the filiform apparatus
the central cell through a germ pore

solution.key_concept: The filiform apparatus of the synergids guides the pollen tube.
steps: The pollen tube grows down the stigma and style and enters the ovule through the micropyle.
It then enters one synergid through the filiform apparatus.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): one of the synergids through the filiform apparatus
solution.why_not_others: The tube enters through the micropyle, not the chalaza. The antipodals lie at the chalazal end. A germ pore is the point where the tube leaves the pollen grain, not a feature of the central cell.
solution.common_trap: Assuming the pollen tube enters the egg directly.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Dioecious; prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Genetic mechanism that inhibits germination or tube growth of self-pollen

solution.key_concept: Outbreeding devices and the techniques of artificial hybridization.
steps: Self-incompatibility is a genetic block on self-pollen: A-III.
Emasculation is the removal of anthers: B-II.
Castor is monoecious and prevents autogamy only: C-IV.
Papaya is dioecious and prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy: D-I.
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps A and B. Option 2 swaps castor and papaya. Option 3 swaps self-incompatibility and papaya.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging the monoecious (castor) and dioecious (papaya) examples.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about outbreeding devices and pollen-pistil interaction are correct?

statements.A: Self-incompatibility prevents self-pollen from the same flower but not pollen from other flowers of the same plant.
statements.B: Non-synchrony of pollen release and stigma receptivity is an outbreeding device.
statements.C: In pollen-pistil interaction, the pistil recognises compatible pollen through chemical components of the pollen and the pistil.
statements.E: After artificial pollen is dusted on the stigma of an emasculated flower, the flower is rebagged.

solution.key_concept: Outbreeding mechanisms, pollen-pistil recognition and the bagging technique.
steps: A is wrong: self-incompatibility blocks self-pollen from the same flower and from other flowers of the same plant.
B is correct: non-synchrony is a listed outbreeding device.
C is correct: recognition depends on chemical components of the pollen and the pistil.
D is wrong: monoecious maize prevents only autogamy, not geitonogamy.
E is correct: the flower is rebagged after pollination.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): B, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 2 and 3 each include A or D, and both of these are false.
solution.common_trap: Thinking self-incompatibility acts only within a single flower, or that monoecy prevents geitonogamy.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: In the embryo sac of an angiosperm, the fusion of a male gamete with the two polar nuclei of the central cell is called:

solution.key_concept: One male gamete fuses with the egg. This is syngamy. The other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei. This is triple fusion.
steps: Triple fusion involves three haploid nuclei: one male gamete and two polar nuclei.
It forms the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN).
Syngamy together with triple fusion makes up double fertilization.
solution.why_not_others: Syngamy is the fusion of a male gamete with the egg. Double fertilization is the name for both fusions together. Parthenocarpy is fruit formation without fertilization.
solution.common_trap: Calling this single fusion 'double fertilization', which is the term for both fusions taken together.
solution.time_saving_tip: Count the nuclei. Three nuclei fuse, so it is triple fusion.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: The leaf cells of an angiosperm contain 24 chromosomes. How many chromosomes will be present in its primary endosperm nucleus?

solution.key_concept: The endosperm is triploid. It forms from one male gamete ($n$) plus two polar nuclei ($2n$).
steps: Leaf cells are diploid, so $2n = 24$ and $n = 12$.
PEN $= n_{male} + 2n_{polar} = 3n$.
solution.why_not_others: 24 assumes the endosperm is diploid. 12 is the gamete number. 48 treats the endosperm as $4n$.
solution.common_trap: Taking the endosperm as diploid like the zygote.
solution.time_saving_tip: Endosperm number = 1.5 times the somatic number.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: A fruit contains 50 seeds, each formed from a fertilized ovule by double fertilization. What is the minimum number of male gametes involved in forming these seeds?

solution.key_concept: Each fertilized ovule uses two male gametes, one for syngamy and one for triple fusion.
steps: Male gametes required $= 2 \times$ number of seeds.
solution.why_not_others: 50 is the number of pollen grains, not male gametes. 25 halves the seed number instead of doubling it. 200 wrongly assumes four gametes per ovule.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the number of pollen grains (one per ovule) with the number of male gametes (two per ovule).
solution.time_saving_tip: Pollen grains = seeds. Male gametes = 2 times the seeds.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: In angiosperms, the primary endosperm nucleus is triploid.
statements.R: The zygote formed by syngamy is diploid and develops into the embryo.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: The PEN is $3n$ because it comes from triple fusion. The zygote ($2n$) comes from a separate fusion.
steps: A is true. The PEN forms from one male gamete plus two polar nuclei, giving $3n$.
R is true. Syngamy of a male gamete with the egg gives a $2n$ zygote, which becomes the embryo.
R describes the other fusion and does not explain why the PEN is triploid.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 is wrong because the ploidy of the zygote does not explain the triploidy of the PEN. Options 3 and 4 are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.common_trap: Linking two true facts about double fertilization as cause and effect.
solution.time_saving_tip: Ask whether R mentions the polar nuclei. It does not, so it cannot explain $3n$.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: The pollen tube releases two male gametes into the cytoplasm of a synergid, and one pollen grain is enough to fertilize one ovule.
statements.II: If the endosperm of a plant has 45 chromosomes, the egg cell of the same plant has 30 chromosomes.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: One pollen grain carries 2 male gametes, enough for one ovule. The endosperm is $3n$ and the egg is $n$.
steps: Statement I is correct as stated in double fertilization.
For Statement II, endosperm $3n = 45$, so $n = 15$.
The egg is haploid and has 15 chromosomes, not 30. 30 is the $2n$ value.
So Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II gives the diploid number for the egg. Statement I is fully correct.
solution.common_trap: Dividing 45 by 3 and then doubling, which treats the egg as diploid.
solution.time_saving_tip: Egg number = endosperm number divided by 3.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Post-fertilization events: endosperm, embryo, seed and fruit
questions.question: After fertilization in angiosperms, which part of the ovule develops into the seed coats?

solution.key_concept: Ovule becomes the seed, integuments become the seed coats, ovary becomes the fruit, and the ovary wall becomes the pericarp.
steps: The integuments surround the ovule.
After fertilization they harden into the seed coats.
solution.why_not_others: The ovary wall becomes the pericarp. A persistent nucellus becomes the perisperm. The thalamus forms part of false fruits.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the ovary wall (which becomes the pericarp) with the integuments (which become the seed coats).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Post-fertilization events: endosperm, embryo, seed and fruit
questions.question: In which of the following is the endosperm retained in the mature seed, making it albuminous?

solution.key_concept: Albuminous seeds keep their endosperm. Non-albuminous seeds use it up before maturity.
steps: Pea, groundnut and beans consume the endosperm fully, so they are non-albuminous.
Castor retains its endosperm, so it is albuminous.
solution.why_not_others: Pea, groundnut and beans are all examples of exalbuminous seeds.
solution.common_trap: Assuming all dicot seeds are non-albuminous. Castor is a dicot with a persistent endosperm.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember the albuminous list: wheat, maize, barley, castor, coconut.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Post-fertilization events: endosperm, embryo, seed and fruit
questions.question: In a monocot embryo, the radicle and root cap are enclosed in a sheath called the:

solution.key_concept: In a monocot embryo, the radicle is enclosed in the coleorhiza and the plumule in the coleoptile.
steps: 'Rhiza' refers to root, so the coleorhiza covers the radicle.
The coleoptile covers the plumule. The scutellum is the single cotyledon.
solution.why_not_others: The coleoptile sheathes the plumule. The scutellum is the cotyledon. The epicotyl is the axis part ending in the plumule.
solution.common_trap: Swapping coleoptile and coleorhiza.
solution.time_saving_tip: Rhiza = root, so coleorhiza covers the radicle.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Post-fertilization events: endosperm, embryo, seed and fruit
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_I.label: D
list_I.text: Seed that germinated after about 10,000 years

solution.key_concept: These are standard examples of seed and fruit features.
steps: Perisperm is persistent nucellus, as in black pepper, so A-III.
A false fruit develops from the thalamus, as in apple, so B-I.
Coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm, so C-IV.
Lupinus arcticus seed germinated after about 10,000 years, so D-II.
solution.why_not_others: Option 2 swaps perisperm and false fruit. Option 3 swaps coconut water and Lupinus. Option 4 assigns coconut water to perisperm, but it is endosperm.
solution.common_trap: Thinking coconut water is perisperm, or treating the white kernel and the water as the same type of endosperm.
solution.time_saving_tip: Fix the most certain pair first (Lupinus with D), then eliminate options.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Post-fertilization events: endosperm, embryo, seed and fruit
questions.question: Which of the following statements about post-fertilization events are correct?

statements.B: In coconut, the white kernel is free-nuclear endosperm.
statements.C: Perisperm is persistent nucellus and is diploid.
statements.D: In a dicot embryo, the hypocotyl terminates in the plumule.
statements.E: Mature seeds generally contain about 10-15% moisture.

options: A, C, D and E only

solution.key_concept: Covers the sequence of endosperm and embryo development, ploidy of seed parts and embryo structure.
steps: A is correct. Endosperm always develops first.
B is incorrect. The kernel is cellular endosperm; the water is free-nuclear endosperm.
C is correct. Perisperm is nucellar tissue and is $2n$.
D is incorrect. The hypocotyl ends in the radicle; the epicotyl ends in the plumule.
E is correct. Mature seeds have about 10-15% moisture.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 2 include B, which is false. Options 2 and 4 include D, which is false.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up epicotyl/plumule with hypocotyl/radicle, and the kernel with the water in coconut.
solution.time_saving_tip: Spot that B and D are false; only option 3 excludes both.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: The formation of a fruit without fertilization, giving seedless fruits, is called:

solution.key_concept: Parthenocarpy is fruit formation without fertilization, as in banana.
steps: No fertilization occurs, so no seeds form.
Banana is the classic example, and growth hormones can induce it.
solution.why_not_others: Apomixis produces seeds, not seedless fruits, without fertilization. Polyembryony means more than one embryo per seed. Syngamy is the fusion of a male gamete with the egg.
solution.common_trap: Confusing apomixis (seeds without fertilization) with parthenocarpy (fruits without fertilization).

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: The occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed, often arising from nucellar cells, is commonly seen in:

solution.key_concept: Polyembryony from nucellar embryos occurs in Citrus and mango.
steps: Polyembryony means more than one embryo per seed.
Citrus is a standard example.
solution.why_not_others: Banana is an example of parthenocarpy. Wheat is an example of an albuminous seed. Groundnut is an example of a non-albuminous seed.
solution.common_trap: Choosing banana by confusing parthenocarpy with polyembryony.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember polyembryony as Citrus and mango.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Crop scientists aim to introduce apomictic genes into hybrid varieties mainly because:
options: the offspring would then show greater genetic variation than the parents
seedless fruits could then be produced without hormone application
the endosperm of such seeds would become triploid
hybrid characters would not segregate, so farmers could reuse the seed each year

solution.key_concept: Hybrid characters segregate in the next generation, so hybrid seed must be bought fresh every year. Apomictic hybrids would not segregate.
steps: Apomixis produces seeds without fertilization, so the offspring are clones.
Clones keep the hybrid traits unchanged.
Farmers could therefore save and resow the hybrid seed.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): hybrid characters would not segregate, so farmers could reuse the seed each year
solution.why_not_others: Apomixis produces clones, which reduces variation rather than increasing it. Seedless fruits come from parthenocarpy. Triploid endosperm results from fertilization, not from apomixis.
solution.common_trap: Thinking apomixis increases variation. It is asexual and gives clones.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Offspring produced by apomixis are clones of the parent plant.
statements.R: In apomixis, seeds are formed without fertilization, for example from a diploid egg cell formed without reduction division.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Apomixis is asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction.
steps: Without meiosis and fertilization, no new combination of genes arises.
The embryo therefore has the same genetic makeup as the parent, making it a clone.
So R correctly explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: R directly accounts for the clonal nature, so option 2 is wrong. Both statements are true, so options 3 and 4 are wrong.
solution.common_trap: Assuming any seed must come from sexual reproduction and so must vary.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In one route of apomixis, cells of the nucellus or integument divide and protrude into the embryo sac to develop into embryos.
statements.II: Parthenocarpy can be induced by applying growth hormones and results in seedless fruits.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Both apomixis and parthenocarpy bypass fertilization, but they produce different products.
steps: Statement I correctly describes the route of apomixis that starts from nucellus or integument cells.
Statement II is correct. Parthenocarpic fruits are seedless and can be induced by growth hormones.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Neither statement contains an error.
solution.common_trap: Believing nucellar embryos form only in polyembryony and not in apomixis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: The scrotum helps maintain the temperature of the testes below the normal body temperature by about:

solution.key_concept: Spermatogenesis needs a temperature 2-2.5 degrees C below body temperature.
steps: The testes lie outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum.
This keeps them 2-2.5 degrees C cooler than the body.
solution.why_not_others: The other ranges are not the stated value.
solution.common_trap: Confusing this value with the size of the testis (4-5 cm long, 2-3 cm wide).

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly shows the sequence of ducts through which sperms pass after leaving the seminiferous tubules?
options: Vasa efferentia → rete testis → epididymis → vas deferens
Rete testis → epididymis → vasa efferentia → vas deferens
Rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens
Rete testis → vasa efferentia → vas deferens → epididymis

solution.key_concept: The male duct pathway is seminiferous tubules, rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis, vas deferens, ejaculatory duct, urethra.
steps: The rete testis comes first, followed by the vasa efferentia.
The vasa efferentia lead into the epididymis, which continues as the vas deferens.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 reverses the first two ducts. Option 2 places the epididymis before the vasa efferentia. Option 4 places the vas deferens before the epididymis.
solution.common_trap: Swapping rete testis and vasa efferentia.
solution.time_saving_tip: Recall the order as 'R-V-E-V': Rete, Vasa efferentia, Epididymis, Vas deferens.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which layer of the uterine wall exhibits strong contractions during parturition?

solution.key_concept: The uterine wall has three layers: perimetrium, myometrium and endometrium.
steps: The myometrium is the muscular middle layer.
It contracts strongly during parturition.
solution.why_not_others: The endometrium undergoes cyclical changes in the menstrual cycle. The perimetrium is the outer layer. Fimbriae belong to the infundibulum of the oviduct, not the uterine wall.
solution.common_trap: Choosing the endometrium, which is the layer that changes cyclically, not the one that contracts.
solution.time_saving_tip: 'Myo' means muscle, and muscle contracts.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Undergoes cyclical changes during the menstrual cycle

solution.key_concept: Each structure is matched to its stated function or feature.
steps: Bulbourethral secretion lubricates the penis, so A-II.
Each testicular lobule has 1-3 seminiferous tubules, so B-IV.
The endometrium changes cyclically, so C-III.
The myometrium contracts in parturition, so D-I.
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps the two uterine layers. Option 2 swaps the bulbourethral gland and the lobule. Option 3 gives the cyclical change to the gland.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the functions of the endometrium and myometrium.
solution.time_saving_tip: A-II and B-IV are easy to fix first; then only options 1 and 4 remain.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about human reproductive systems are correct?

statements.A: Each testis has about 250 testicular lobules.
statements.B: The prostate is a paired accessory gland of the male.
statements.C: Seminal plasma is rich in fructose, calcium and enzymes.
statements.D: The ampulla is a part of the male duct system lying between the epididymis and the vas deferens.
statements.E: Milk passes from the mammary tubules to the mammary duct, then to the mammary ampulla and finally to the lactiferous duct.

options: A, B, C and E only

solution.key_concept: Covers the structure of the testis, the accessory glands, the parts of the oviduct and the mammary duct sequence.
steps: A is correct. There are about 250 lobules per testis.
B is incorrect. The prostate is single; the seminal vesicles and bulbourethral glands are paired.
C is correct. Seminal plasma is rich in fructose, calcium and enzymes.
D is incorrect. The ampulla is a part of the oviduct; the epididymis leads directly into the vas deferens.
E is correct. This is the stated mammary duct sequence.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options 2 and 4 include B, which is false, and option 2 also includes D, which is false. Option 1 omits the correct statement E.
solution.common_trap: Placing oviduct parts such as the ampulla or infundibulum in the male system, and thinking the prostate is paired.
solution.time_saving_tip: Rule out B and D, then check whether E is true.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microscopic anatomy of testis and ovary
questions.question: Which cells of the human testis synthesise and secrete androgens such as testosterone?

solution.key_concept: Leydig cells lie in the interstitial spaces outside the seminiferous tubules and secrete androgens.
steps: Androgens such as testosterone are made by the Leydig (interstitial) cells.
Sertoli cells nourish germ cells, and spermatogonia are germ cells.
Granulosa cells belong to ovarian follicles.
solution.why_not_others: Sertoli cells nourish germ cells. Spermatogonia undergo meiosis to form sperm. Granulosa cells surround oocytes in the ovary.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the roles of Sertoli and Leydig cells.
solution.time_saving_tip: Think of Leydig cells as the hormone makers and Sertoli cells as the nurse cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microscopic anatomy of testis and ovary
questions.question: In which stage of ovarian follicle development does the fluid-filled antrum first appear?

solution.key_concept: The antrum is first seen in the tertiary follicle.
steps: A primary follicle is a primary oocyte surrounded by granulosa cells.
A secondary follicle has more granulosa layers and a new theca, but no antrum.
A tertiary follicle has a fluid-filled antrum, and its theca is organised into theca interna and theca externa.
solution.why_not_others: Primary and secondary follicles lack an antrum. The corpus luteum forms from follicle remnants after ovulation.
solution.common_trap: Thinking the antrum appears as soon as the theca forms, which happens in the secondary follicle.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microscopic anatomy of testis and ovary
questions.question: Which of the following is found in the interstitial spaces outside the seminiferous tubules rather than in the lining inside them?

solution.key_concept: The tubule lining contains germ cells and Sertoli cells. The interstitial spaces contain blood vessels, immunocompetent cells and Leydig cells.
steps: The inside of each seminiferous tubule is lined by male germ cells and Sertoli cells.
The interstitial spaces hold small blood vessels, immunocompetent cells and Leydig cells.
So immunocompetent cells lie outside the tubules.
solution.why_not_others: Spermatogonia, Sertoli cells and meiotic germ cells all line the inside of the tubules.
solution.common_trap: Placing Sertoli cells in the interstitium together with Leydig cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microscopic anatomy of testis and ovary
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: A fluid-filled antrum is a characteristic feature of the primary follicle.
statements.R: A tertiary follicle has a fluid-filled antrum, and its theca is organised into theca interna and theca externa.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: The antrum first appears in the tertiary follicle, not the primary follicle.
steps: A primary follicle is only a primary oocyte surrounded by granulosa cells, with no antrum, so A is false.
A tertiary follicle has an antrum and a theca organised into theca interna and theca externa, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so options 1, 2 and 3 cannot be correct.
solution.common_trap: Assuming all follicle stages have an antrum.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microscopic anatomy of testis and ovary
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Sertoli cells, which nourish germ cells, line the inside of the seminiferous tubules, whereas androgen-secreting Leydig cells lie in the interstitial spaces outside the tubules.
statements.II: In a secondary follicle, the primary oocyte is surrounded by more layers of granulosa cells and a new theca, but no antrum is present yet.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Testis: Sertoli cells are inside the tubules and Leydig cells are outside. Ovary: the antrum appears only at the tertiary stage.
steps: Sertoli cells line the tubules and nourish germ cells, while Leydig cells in the interstitium secrete androgens, so Statement I is correct.
A secondary follicle has more granulosa layers and a new theca, and the antrum forms only in the tertiary follicle, so Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Each statement matches the described histology, so no option that marks either one incorrect can be right.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that the appearance of the theca coincides with the antrum.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: How many chromosomes does a human secondary spermatocyte contain?

solution.key_concept: Meiosis I halves the chromosome number, so secondary spermatocytes are haploid.
steps: Spermatogonia and primary spermatocytes are $2n = 46$.
Meiosis I produces two secondary spermatocytes with $n = 23$.
solution.why_not_others: 46 is the number in spermatogonia and primary spermatocytes. 92 and 69 do not occur at any normal stage.
solution.common_trap: Thinking haploidy is reached only after meiosis II.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: How many functional gametes are formed in total from 40 primary spermatocytes and 40 primary oocytes?

solution.key_concept: $1$ primary spermatocyte gives $4$ sperms, while $1$ primary oocyte gives only $1$ ovum plus polar bodies.
steps: Sperms: $40 \times 4 = 160$.
Ova: $40 \times 1 = 40$, because unequal cytokinesis gives polar bodies instead of extra ova.
solution.why_not_others: 160 ova assumes oogenesis also gives four gametes. 80 sperms stops at the secondary spermatocyte count. 120 ova wrongly adds polar bodies as functional gametes.
solution.common_trap: Counting polar bodies as ova.
solution.time_saving_tip: Multiply spermatocytes by 4; the number of oocytes equals the number of ova.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: In the hormonal control of spermatogenesis, LH and FSH act respectively on which cells?

solution.key_concept: GnRH raises LH and FSH. LH stimulates androgen secretion by Leydig cells, and FSH acts on Sertoli cells.
steps: LH acts on Leydig cells to stimulate androgen synthesis.
FSH acts on Sertoli cells to promote factors that aid spermiogenesis.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Leydig cells and Sertoli cells
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 reverses the targets. Spermatogonia are not named as the direct target of either hormone.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the LH and FSH targets.
solution.time_saving_tip: Link the letters: LH goes with Leydig cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Release of sperm from the seminiferous tubules

solution.key_concept: Spermiogenesis transforms spermatids and spermiation releases sperm. The acrosome aids fertilisation, and the middle piece holds mitochondria.
steps: Spermiogenesis converts spermatids into spermatozoa, so A-III.
Spermiation releases sperm from the tubules, so B-I.
The acrosome helps fertilisation, so C-IV.
The middle piece is packed with mitochondria, so D-II.
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 4 swap spermiogenesis with spermiation. Options 3 and 4 swap the roles of the acrosome and the middle piece.
solution.common_trap: Confusing spermiogenesis with spermiation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about gametogenesis in humans are correct?

statements.A: Oogenesis begins during foetal life, whereas spermatogenesis begins at puberty.
statements.B: New oogonia continue to be added to the ovary after birth until puberty.
statements.C: The primary oocyte remains arrested in prophase I until puberty.
statements.D: Completion of meiosis I by the primary oocyte gives a secondary oocyte and a first polar body of nearly equal size.
statements.E: For normal fertility, at least 60% of sperm should have normal shape and at least 40% should show vigorous motility.

solution.key_concept: Oogenesis starts in the foetus, no oogonia are added after birth, and cytokinesis in the oocyte is unequal.
steps: A is correct: oogenesis is foetal and spermatogenesis starts at puberty.
B is incorrect: no oogonia are added after birth.
C is correct: the primary oocyte is arrested in prophase I.
D is incorrect: the secondary oocyte is large and the first polar body is tiny.
E is correct: these are the stated fertility criteria.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Every other combination includes B or D, and both are false.
solution.common_trap: Assuming meiotic divisions in oogenesis are equal, as they are in spermatogenesis.
solution.time_saving_tip: Rejecting B alone rules out options 1 and 4.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: The rupture of the Graafian follicle around the middle of the menstrual cycle is induced by a surge of which hormone?

solution.key_concept: The mid-cycle LH surge causes ovulation.
steps: LH and FSH peak around day 14.
The LH surge induces rupture of the Graafian follicle, which is ovulation.
solution.why_not_others: Progesterone dominates the luteal phase after ovulation. Estrogen peaks before ovulation but does not itself rupture the follicle. hCG is a placental hormone.
solution.common_trap: Choosing estrogen because it peaks just before ovulation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: A woman has regular menstrual cycles of 32 days. Assuming a constant luteal phase, on approximately which day of her cycle does ovulation occur?

solution.key_concept: Ovulation day $\approx$ cycle length $- 14$, because the luteal phase lasts about 14 days.
steps: Ovulation day $\approx 32 - 14$.
solution.why_not_others: Day 14 applies only to a 28-day cycle. Day 16 comes from halving the cycle length. Day 20 is an arithmetic error.
solution.common_trap: Assuming ovulation always occurs on day 14 or at exactly mid-cycle.
solution.time_saving_tip: Subtract 14 from the cycle length.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: During the secretory phase of the menstrual cycle, which hormone maintains the endometrium for implantation, and what is its main source?

solution.key_concept: The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, which maintains the endometrium.
steps: After ovulation, the follicle remnants form the corpus luteum.
The corpus luteum secretes mainly progesterone, which maintains the endometrium.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Progesterone from the corpus luteum
solution.why_not_others: Estrogen from the follicle regenerates the endometrium in the proliferative phase. The corpus luteum does not mainly secrete estrogen. LH comes from the pituitary, not the corpus luteum.
solution.common_trap: Thinking the corpus luteum mainly secretes estrogen.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: During the follicular phase, the endometrium regenerates mainly under the influence of progesterone secreted by the corpus luteum.
statements.R: The growing ovarian follicles secrete estrogen during the follicular phase.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: In the proliferative phase, follicular estrogen regenerates the endometrium. The corpus luteum forms only after ovulation.
steps: The corpus luteum does not yet exist in the follicular phase, and estrogen, not progesterone, regenerates the endometrium, so A is false.
Growing follicles secrete estrogen, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, which rules out options 1, 2 and 3.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up which hormone controls which phase.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In the absence of fertilisation, the corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone levels fall, and menstruation follows.
statements.II: Estrogen level reaches its peak during the luteal phase, after the corpus luteum has formed.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Estrogen peaks before ovulation. A fall in progesterone triggers menstruation.
steps: Statement I matches the notes: corpus luteum degeneration lowers progesterone and leads to menstruation, so it is correct.
Estrogen peaks before ovulation, not in the luteal phase, so Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II is false, which rules out options 1 and 4. Statement I is true, which rules out option 2.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that because the corpus luteum secretes hormones, estrogen must peak in the luteal phase.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Fertilisation, embryo development up to blastocyst and implantation
questions.question: In humans, fertilisation normally takes place at the:

solution.key_concept: Fertilisation occurs at the ampullary-isthmic junction of the oviduct.
steps: The sperm meets the secondary oocyte in the oviduct at the ampullary-isthmic junction.
The endometrium is the site of implantation, not fertilisation.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Ampullary-isthmic junction of the oviduct
solution.why_not_others: The endometrium is where implantation occurs. The infundibulum and cervix are not stated sites of fertilisation.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the site of fertilisation with the site of implantation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Fertilisation, embryo development up to blastocyst and implantation
questions.question: The morula stage of the human embryo consists of how many blastomeres?

solution.key_concept: The morula is the 8-16 cell embryo.
steps: Mitotic cleavage of the zygote produces blastomeres.
The embryo with 8-16 blastomeres is called the morula, which then becomes the blastocyst.
solution.why_not_others: 2-4 and 4-8 are earlier cleavage stages. 32-64 is not the stated range for the morula.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the morula range with the 'up to 8 blastomeres' limit used for ZIFT.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Fertilisation, embryo development up to blastocyst and implantation
questions.question: Which part of the human blastocyst attaches to the endometrium at the start of implantation?

solution.key_concept: The outer trophoblast of the blastocyst attaches to the endometrium.
steps: The blastocyst has an outer trophoblast and an inner cell mass.
The trophoblast attaches to the endometrium, and the uterine cells then cover the blastocyst.
solution.why_not_others: The inner cell mass contains the stem cells that form the embryo. The zona pellucida covers the oocyte. The second polar body is a by-product of meiosis II.
solution.common_trap: Choosing the inner cell mass because it forms the embryo.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Fertilisation, embryo development up to blastocyst and implantation
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Stem cells that give rise to all tissues and organs

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Help the sperm enter the cytoplasm of the secondary oocyte

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Diploid cell formed by fusion of haploid nuclei

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Membrane changes on sperm contact with the zona pellucida that prevent entry of additional sperm

solution.key_concept: Fertilisation events and the parts of the early embryo.
steps: The zygote is the diploid cell formed by fusion of haploid nuclei, so A-III.
Acrosomal enzymes help sperm entry, so B-II.
The inner cell mass contains stem cells, so C-I.
Membrane changes on contact with the zona pellucida block polyspermy, so D-IV.
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps the zygote with the inner cell mass. Option 3 swaps acrosomal enzymes with the polyspermy block. Option 4 swaps the zygote with the polyspermy block.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the role of acrosomal enzymes with the block to polyspermy.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Fertilisation, embryo development up to blastocyst and implantation
questions.question: Which of the following statements about fertilisation and early embryonic development are correct?

statements.A: The sex of the baby is decided by the ovum.
statements.B: The secondary oocyte completes meiosis II after sperm entry, forming the ovum and a second polar body.
statements.C: The zygote undergoes meiotic cleavage as it moves toward the uterus.
statements.D: The blastocyst becomes embedded in the endometrium after uterine cells cover it, and this is called implantation.
statements.E: The blastocyst has an outer trophoblast and an inner cell mass.

solution.key_concept: The sperm decides sex, cleavage is mitotic, and meiosis II is completed only after sperm entry.
steps: A is incorrect: sex is decided by the sperm (X or Y).
B is correct: meiosis II is completed after sperm entry.
C is incorrect: cleavage is mitotic.
D is correct: this embedding is implantation.
E is correct: the blastocyst has a trophoblast and an inner cell mass.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): B, D and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 2 and 3 each include A or C, and both are false.
solution.common_trap: Believing the oocyte completes meiosis before ovulation, or calling cleavage meiotic.
solution.time_saving_tip: Rejecting A and C leaves only option 4.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Pregnancy, placenta formation, parturition and lactation
questions.question: The first milk secreted by the mother after childbirth gives passive immunity to the newborn. Which antibodies is it particularly rich in?

solution.key_concept: Colostrum, the first milk, contains IgA antibodies that give passive immunity to the newborn.
steps: The first milk after parturition is called colostrum.
Colostrum is rich in IgA antibodies.
These antibodies give the infant passive immunity.
solution.why_not_others: IgE, IgM and IgD are not the antibodies that characterise colostrum.
solution.common_trap: Picking another antibody class because it sounds familiar; colostrum is specifically linked with IgA.
solution.time_saving_tip: Link the words colostrum and IgA together.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Pregnancy, placenta formation, parturition and lactation
questions.question: During human pregnancy, the first movements of the foetus and the appearance of hair on its head are usually seen during which month?

solution.key_concept: Timeline of foetal development during pregnancy.
steps: The heart forms after one month.
Limbs and digits form by the end of the second month.
Most organ systems have formed by the end of 12 weeks.
First foetal movements and hair on the head appear in the fifth month.
solution.why_not_others: The second month is the stage of limb and digit formation. The third month ends the first trimester, when organ systems form. By the end of 24 weeks, eyelids separate and eyelashes form.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the fifth-month milestones with those at the end of the first trimester or at 24 weeks.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember: 5th month gives movement and head hair.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Pregnancy, placenta formation, parturition and lactation
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: The signals that start parturition come from the maternal hypothalamus, independently of the foetus.
statements.R: During parturition, oxytocin acts on the uterine myometrium and causes stronger uterine contractions.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Parturition is started by the foetal ejection reflex, which comes from the fully developed foetus and placenta.
steps: The foetal ejection reflex comes from the fully developed foetus and placenta, so A is false.
This reflex triggers oxytocin release.
Oxytocin acts on the myometrium and causes stronger contractions, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so options 1, 2 and 3 cannot be correct.
solution.common_trap: Assuming labour is started only by the mother's brain; the signal comes from the foetus and placenta.
solution.time_saving_tip: Foetal ejection reflex is named after its source, the foetus.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Pregnancy, placenta formation, parturition and lactation
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: By the end of 12 weeks of pregnancy, the eyelids of the foetus separate and the eyelashes are formed.
statements.II: The finger-like chorionic villi that help form the placenta grow from the inner cell mass.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Placenta formation and the timeline of foetal development.
steps: Eyelids separating and eyelashes forming happen by the end of 24 weeks, not 12 weeks, so Statement I is incorrect.
By 12 weeks, most organ systems, limbs and external genitalia have formed.
Chorionic villi grow from the trophoblast, so Statement II is incorrect.
The inner cell mass differentiates into ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Neither statement is correct, so options 1, 3 and 4 are ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the trophoblast with the inner cell mass, and the 12-week milestones with the 24-week ones.
solution.time_saving_tip: Trophoblast gives the placenta; inner cell mass gives the embryo.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Reproductive health and prevention of STDs
questions.question: Sexually transmitted infections are most common among persons of which age group?

solution.key_concept: STIs have their highest incidence in the 15-24 years age group.
steps: Recall the age group in which STIs are most common.
It is 15-24 years.
solution.why_not_others: The other age groups do not have the highest incidence of STIs.
solution.common_trap: Choosing the 25-34 years group by assuming sexual activity peaks later.
solution.time_saving_tip: 15-24 years is the youth bracket.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Reproductive health and prevention of STDs
questions.question: Which of the following sexually transmitted infections is NOT completely curable, even when detected early and treated properly?

solution.key_concept: Hepatitis B, genital herpes and HIV are not completely curable. The other common STIs are curable if detected early.
steps: Recall the three STIs that are not completely curable: hepatitis B, genital herpes and HIV.
Of the options given, only genital herpes is in this group.
solution.why_not_others: Gonorrhoea, syphilis and trichomoniasis are completely curable if detected early.
solution.common_trap: Thinking syphilis is incurable because it is a serious disease.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember the incurable trio: hepatitis B, herpes, HIV.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Reproductive health and prevention of STDs
questions.question: Which pair of infections can be transmitted not only sexually but also by sharing injection needles, by transfusion of infected blood and from an infected mother to the foetus?

solution.key_concept: Hepatitis B and HIV are also spread by sharing needles, by blood transfusion and from mother to foetus.
steps: Find the STIs that also spread through needles, blood and from mother to foetus.
These are hepatitis B and HIV.
solution.why_not_others: None of the other pairs is described as spreading through these additional routes.
solution.common_trap: Choosing genital herpes because it is also incurable. It is not one of the infections spread by these routes.
solution.time_saving_tip: Blood-borne STIs: hepatitis B and HIV.

questions.subject: biology

solution.common_trap: Thinking LNG-20 is a copper device because its name contains a number, like Multiload 375.

questions.question: Lactational amenorrhea, used as a natural method of contraception, is considered effective for up to how long after parturition?

steps: While the mother breastfeeds intensely, menstrual cycles are absent.
This method is effective for up to 6 months after parturition.

questions.question: Under the MTP (Amendment) Act 2017, termination of pregnancy between 12 and 24 weeks requires the opinion of how many registered medical practitioners?

solution.key_concept: The MTP (Amendment) Act 2017 sets how many medical opinions are needed at each stage of pregnancy.
steps: Termination within 12 weeks needs the opinion of one registered medical practitioner.
Termination between 12 and 24 weeks needs the opinion of two.
solution.why_not_others: One opinion is the rule for pregnancies within 12 weeks. Three opinions, or none, are not what the Act requires.
solution.common_trap: Applying the single-opinion rule for pregnancies within 12 weeks to the 12-24 week period.
solution.time_saving_tip: Later stage of pregnancy means more opinions: one, then two.

statements.A: Hormone-releasing IUDs such as Progestasert and LNG-20 help prevent pregnancy.
statements.R: Hormone-releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperm.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

solution.key_concept: How hormone-releasing IUDs work.
steps: Progestasert and LNG-20 are hormone-releasing IUDs used for contraception, so A is true.
They make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperm, so R is true.
These effects are exactly how they prevent pregnancy, so R explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true and directly linked, so options 2, 3 and 4 are ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Giving hormonal IUDs the copper IUD action of suppressing sperm motility.
solution.time_saving_tip: Hormonal IUDs act on the uterus and cervix; copper IUDs act on sperm.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Copper-releasing IUDs such as CuT work by making the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperm, and they do not affect sperm motility.
statements.II: Emergency contraceptive pills are effective if taken within 7 days of unprotected coitus.

steps: Copper-releasing IUDs suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity, so Statement I is incorrect.
Making the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperm is how hormonal IUDs work.
Emergency contraception is effective within 72 hours of coitus, not 7 days, so Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are false, so options 1, 3 and 4 are ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the actions of copper and hormonal IUDs, or overestimating the time window for emergency contraception.
solution.time_saving_tip: Emergency contraception window: 72 hours, which is 3 days.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: In amniocentesis, which material is analysed?
options: Foetal cells and dissolved substances in the amniotic fluid
Maternal blood cells taken from an arm vein
Cells scraped from the uterine endometrium
Colostrum collected from the mammary glands

solution.key_concept: Amniocentesis analyses a sample of amniotic fluid.
steps: A small sample of the amniotic fluid around the foetus is withdrawn.
The foetal cells and dissolved substances in it are analysed.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Foetal cells and dissolved substances in the amniotic fluid
solution.why_not_others: Maternal blood, endometrial cells and colostrum are not sampled in amniocentesis.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that prenatal diagnosis uses maternal tissue rather than foetal material.
solution.time_saving_tip: The name says it: amnio refers to amniotic fluid.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Why is the use of amniocentesis for determining the sex of the foetus legally banned in India?
options: Amniocentesis cannot reveal the sex of the foetus
Amniocentesis can detect only metabolic disorders and not chromosomes
Amniocentesis is used only after birth of the child
Its misuse for sex determination led to female foeticide

solution.key_concept: Amniocentesis was misused for sex determination, which led to female foeticide.
steps: The karyotype obtained by amniocentesis reveals the sex of the foetus.
This was misused to find the sex of the foetus, leading to female foeticide.
So its use for sex determination is legally banned in India.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Its misuse for sex determination led to female foeticide
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 is wrong because the karyotype does reveal sex. Option 2 is wrong because it detects chromosomal abnormalities. Option 3 is wrong because it is a prenatal technique.
solution.common_trap: Assuming the ban exists because the test is inaccurate; the ban exists because of misuse.
solution.time_saving_tip: The ban is about misuse, not about technical limits.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which of the following conditions can be detected by amniocentesis?
options: Pelvic inflammatory disease in the mother
Blocked fallopian tubes in the mother
Low sperm count in the father

solution.key_concept: Amniocentesis detects chromosomal abnormalities and some genetic or metabolic disorders of the foetus.
steps: Amniocentesis examines foetal cells in the amniotic fluid.
It can therefore detect foetal chromosomal abnormalities such as Down syndrome.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Down syndrome in the foetus
solution.why_not_others: PID, blocked fallopian tubes and low sperm count are conditions of the parents and are not studied by analysing amniotic fluid.
solution.common_trap: Thinking amniocentesis diagnoses the parents' reproductive problems; it tests only the foetus.
solution.time_saving_tip: Amniocentesis tests the foetus, so choose the foetal condition.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Infertility and assisted reproductive technologies: IVF, ZIFT, GIFT
questions.question: In zygote intra fallopian transfer (ZIFT), where is the zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres placed?

solution.key_concept: ZIFT transfers a zygote or an early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube.
steps: The name gives the site: zygote intra fallopian transfer.
An embryo with up to 8 blastomeres goes into the fallopian tube.
Only embryos with more than 8 blastomeres go into the uterus, and that technique is IUT.
solution.why_not_others: The uterus is the site for IUT, which uses embryos with more than 8 blastomeres. The vagina is a site for artificial insemination, which introduces semen and not an embryo. The cervix is not the transfer site in any of these techniques.
solution.common_trap: Assuming every embryo transfer goes into the uterus. The site depends on the embryo stage.
solution.time_saving_tip: Expand the acronym: the 'F' in ZIFT stands for fallopian.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Infertility and assisted reproductive technologies: IVF, ZIFT, GIFT
questions.question: A woman cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation and development. Which assisted reproductive technique involves transferring an ovum collected from a donor into her fallopian tube?

solution.key_concept: In GIFT, a donor ovum is transferred into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce ova but can support fertilisation and development.
steps: Identify what is transferred: an ovum, which is a gamete, not a zygote.
Identify the site: the fallopian tube.
Transferring a gamete into the fallopian tube is GIFT.
solution.why_not_others: ZIFT transfers a zygote or early embryo, not an ovum. IUI introduces semen into the uterus. ICSI injects a sperm directly into the ovum.
solution.common_trap: Confusing GIFT with ZIFT. GIFT transfers an ovum, while ZIFT transfers a zygote or early embryo.
solution.time_saving_tip: G stands for gamete and Z stands for zygote.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Infertility and assisted reproductive technologies: IVF, ZIFT, GIFT
questions.question: An embryo formed by in vitro fertilisation has 16 blastomeres. Which technique, with the correct transfer site, is used to transfer it?

solution.key_concept: Embryos with up to 8 blastomeres are transferred by ZIFT, and embryos with more than 8 blastomeres by IUT.
steps: Compare the embryo stage with the cut-off: 16 is more than 8.
Apply the rule: more than 8 blastomeres means IUT.
In IUT, the embryo is placed in the uterus.
solution.why_not_others: ZIFT is used only for embryos with up to 8 blastomeres. GIFT transfers an ovum, not an embryo. IUI introduces semen, not an embryo.
solution.common_trap: Choosing IUI because its site is also the uterus. IUI transfers semen, not an embryo.
solution.time_saving_tip: Use the rule: up to 8 blastomeres means ZIFT, more than 8 means IUT.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Infertility and assisted reproductive technologies: IVF, ZIFT, GIFT
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: In GIFT, the recipient female must be able to provide a suitable environment for fertilisation and development.
statements.R: In GIFT, an ovum, and not a zygote, is transferred into the fallopian tube of the recipient female.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: GIFT places an unfertilised donor ovum into the recipient's fallopian tube, so fertilisation and development must happen inside her body.
steps: GIFT is meant for a female who cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation and development, so A is true.
In GIFT, the transferred structure is an ovum, not a zygote, and it is placed in the fallopian tube, so R is true.
An unfertilised ovum is placed in her body, so fertilisation and development must take place there. This is why her internal environment must be suitable.
Therefore R correctly explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: R directly explains why the recipient's environment matters, so option (2) is wrong. Both statements are true, so options (3) and (4) are wrong.
solution.common_trap: Thinking GIFT transfers a zygote, as ZIFT does, and therefore marking R false.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Infertility and assisted reproductive technologies: IVF, ZIFT, GIFT
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: An embryo at the 8-blastomere stage can be transferred into the fallopian tube by ZIFT.
statements.II: In ICSI, semen collected from the husband or a donor is introduced into the uterus of the female.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: ZIFT transfers a zygote or embryo with up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube. ICSI injects a sperm directly into the ovum.
steps: ZIFT accepts embryos with up to 8 blastomeres, and this limit includes 8, so Statement I is correct.
Introducing semen from the husband or a donor into the uterus describes IUI, a form of artificial insemination.
ICSI instead injects a single sperm directly into the ovum, so Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II describes IUI, not ICSI, so options (1) and (4) are wrong. Statement I is correct because 8 blastomeres falls within the ZIFT limit, so option (2) is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Treating the 8-blastomere stage as an IUT case. Only embryos with more than 8 blastomeres go to the uterus.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember 'up to 8' includes 8, and ICSI means sperm into the ovum's cytoplasm.
